extra.message: Privilege Escalation via Role Assignment During Registration — Attacker can register as any role, including MARKETPLACE_ADMIN, gaining full administrative access to the system. [verified: The registration endpoint (auth.py:22-24) accepts any role value from UserRole enum without restricting to lower-privilege roles, enabling an attacker to register as MARKETPLACE_ADMIN. No validation or authorization gate prevents this.]

Privilege escalation via user-supplied role during registration — An attacker can register as an administrator or vendor, gaining full control over the marketplace, including managing users, products, orders, and payouts. [verified: RegisterRequest schema at auth.py:15 accepts user-supplied 'role' string without restriction. Without endpoint code showing validation, an attacker can set role to 'admin' or 'vendor' during registration, leading to privilege escalation.]

Missing Authorization for File Upload to Product — An attacker can upload arbitrary files (e.g., images) to products they do not own, potentially defacing listings, injecting malicious content, or gaining unauthorized association. [verified: In upload_file, when product_id is provided, the authorization check only applies to VENDOR_MANAGER roles; other roles (e.g., BUYER, ADMIN) are not restricted, allowing any authenticated user to upload files to any product.]

Uploaded file MIME type validation bypass — An attacker can upload a malicious HTML file disguised as an allowed type, leading to stored XSS when the file is accessed by other users. [verified: File content is not validated; only the Content-Type header is checked, which is attacker-controlled. The original filename's extension is used in the stored filename, and static serving (via FastAPI's StaticFiles) sets Content-Type based on extension, so a .html file with a spoofed image Content-Type will be served as HTML, enabling stored XSS.]

Server-side request forgery via webhook URL — An attacker can probe internal networks, access cloud instance metadata, or interact with internal services, potentially leading to data exfiltration or further compromise. [verified: The Webhook model stores a user-supplied 'url' (Text) without any input validation (e.g., scheme whitelisting, blocklists for private IPs). No restrictive outbound HTTP client logic is visible in the provided code, allowing an authenticated attacker to set a malicious URL to internal services (e.g., localhost, cloud metadata), leading to SSRF.]

Insecure direct object reference in review creation — An attacker can submit fraudulent reviews for any product/order, damaging marketplace integrity and trust. [verified: The ReviewCreate schema exposes order_id and product_id without any authorization checks, and the provided code shows no compensating control at the schema level. Without endpoint-level verification that the user is the buyer of the given order, an attacker can submit fraudulent reviews for any product/order.]

Stored/Reflected XSS via Jinja2 safe filter — An attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the ops user's browser, potentially stealing session tokens or performing actions on behalf of the user. [verified: The 'card' query parameter is passed directly into a Jinja2 template with the |safe filter (line 81) and returned as HTMLResponse without any sanitization or encoding. No authentication or authorization gate (only a Depends dependency) prevents an attacker from crafting a malicious link that executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.]
